title: A matched bridge's admission threshold sets its bias: at the threshold used in practice the bridged contrast was biased by twice the true effect
question: How do the bias of a matched bridge across a disconnected network and the existence of the bridged comparison depend on the admission threshold, expressed in multiples of the distance between arms of one randomized trial?
design: Two disconnected subnetworks of six trials; cross-gap control arms matched on covariate means at thresholds of 1 to 20 within-trial units; good or poor overlap, an index with or without the most prognostic covariate, study-level heterogeneity absent or present. 8 cells, 2000 replicates each.
answer: No. With trial populations shifted across the gap, the bridged contrast (truth -0.2) was biased by -0.03 at the within-trial arm distance, where the bridge existed in only 8% of replicates, -0.13 at three times it and -0.44 at ten times it, near the threshold used in practice, where it always existed and its interval never covered. An index omitting the most prognostic covariate was biased by -0.25 even at the tightest threshold. Pooling pairs that reuse arms made intervals undercover even without bias (0.76 at ten units with good overlap).
findings: Bias moved by 0.19 to 0.39 across thresholds at which the bridge existed at least a fifth of the time (poor overlap).
Probability the bridge exists at the within-trial distance: 46% (good overlap) and 8% (poor), all covariates in the index.
Study-level baseline heterogeneity (SD 0.1) lowered coverage at every threshold, since no covariate distance sees it.
not_answered: Monte Carlo networks only, no real-network deletions; one distance with two covariate sets; no component network meta-analysis bridge; admitted pairs pooled as independent. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Cross-gap mean difference A versus B through a matched C-D bridge
methods_compared: matched bridge at thresholds of 1 to 20 within-trial distance units, two covariate indices
n_sim: 2000 per cell, 8 cells, 8 thresholds on the same data
